basis: Propagated through PTHR23148, whose five other reviewed members all carry a PWI domain that JIP4 lacks. No experimental yeast dataset places JIP4 in a spliceosomal preparation. JIP4's own domains (PF29926, PF29925) are confined to S. cerevisiae YOR019W and YGR237C.

term: regulation of mRNA splicing, via spliceosome
basis: Same propagation route as GO:0005681. The one (RS)5 repeat at 343-352 is 10 residues inside a disordered insertion and is absent from every established S. cerevisiae SR-like protein tested, so it does not substitute for SR-domain architecture.

The USP fold assignment alone does not imply nucleotide binding. The MJ0577 G-x(2)-G-x(9)-G-[ST] loop is not conserved in JIP4, and transplanting ATP gives 12 clashing heavy atoms against 0 in the control. Many UspA-fold proteins are non-nucleotide-binding.

Structure search assigns a fold (UspA within Pfam clan CL0039) but no activity. The nucleotide site is degenerate and occluded, the second module (PF29925) has no assignable homologue, and no motif class in the disordered 71.5% exceeds a composition-matched null.
No experimental process annotation exists for JIP4. The paralog's mitophagy annotation (GO:0000422) comes from a genome-wide screen and must not be transferred: JIP4 was not a hit.

recommended_action: FLAG TO PANTHER/InterPro as a misassignment (lead)
basis: Removing Q03361 from PTHR23148, or marking it as a non-propagating outlier, removes the source of both IBA terms at once. A UspA-based family (the branch shared with YOR019W, YGR237C and S. pombe P87132) fits the structural evidence.
PubMed searches for JIP4/YDR475C in yeast spliceosome proteomics returned no paper reporting it in a spliceosomal preparation. The statement appears to restate the PANTHER family name.
